actionable_steps.citation: Keep Your Focus On God Constantly — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 26 (1993), 1993-04-18
actionable_steps.step: Switch on the torch of discrimination in the darkness of doubt — look again and see the rope as rope; refuse to feed the snake of imagination.

actionable_steps.citation: Keep Your Focus On God Constantly — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 26 (1993), 1993-04-18
actionable_steps.step: Fill your thoughts with love and walk the path of sacrifice — then illusion can never touch you.
Practise inquiry (vichara) into the nature of the Atma daily — inquiry makes the snake disappear, and only the rope remains.

actionable_steps.citation: The juggler behind this jugglery — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 6 (1966), 1966-09-08
actionable_steps.step: Subdue the juggler with keerthana — concentrated contemplation of the glory of God.

actionable_steps.citation: Reminiscence of the Divine — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 35 (2002), 2002-10-20
actionable_steps.step: Practise letting go of one worldly attachment the way Swami let go of the collar pin — declare inwardly that maya cannot bind you any longer.

definition.citation: Vinayaka worship ranks first — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 24 (1991), 1991-09-12
definition.quote: Maya is the delusion which makes one imagine the presence of that which is not present. … It makes one imagine the presence of what is not there and not perceive what is really there.

discourses.citation: Keep Your Focus On God Constantly — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 26 (1993), 1993-04-18
discourses.quote: Illusion (maya) is, in fact, our own delusion. Otherwise, it has no existence. It is our imagination. … Switch on a torch and see. The rope remains as it is, there is no snake.

discourses.citation: Renunciation and Realisation — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 21 (1988), 1988-07-11
discourses.quote: Maya is the cause of thinking the impermanent as permanent and the permanent as perishable.

discourses.citation: The juggler behind this jugglery — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 6 (1966), 1966-09-08
discourses.quote: The veil of maya (illusion), however, hides from him the face of God which is shining from every being and thing around him. … This na-rtha-ki can be subdued by kee-rtha-na (mark the change of syllables). Keerthana is the concentrated contemplation of the glory of God.

make_it_real: Maya has no hands and no legs — you're the one holding it. Loosen your grip, and catch Brahman instead.
title: Maya / Illusion

vahinis.quote: O King, illusion (maya) itself has caused the multifarious forms. This is clever stage play, a kind of fancy dress.
The idea of the snake, which is an illusion (maya), flourishes on the ignorance of the real nature of the rope; it grows and becomes deeper the more one forgets the rope, which is the base.
